title: A non-retinoid triazolopyrimidine RBP4 antagonist for the treatment of Stargardt disease
abstract: Stargardt disease is a juvenile-onset retinal dystrophy characterized by the buildup of cytotoxic lipofuscin deposits in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), leading to photoreceptor degeneration and eventual blindness. Currently, there are no FDA-approved treatments for Stargardt disease. Bisretinoids, byproducts of the visual cycle, are the major cytotoxic components of the lipofuscin deposits, and bisretinoid synthesis relies on the traffic of retinol from the bloodstream to the retina.

title: AF-RECAL: Multi-Modal Structural Recalibration of AlphaFold 3 Hallucinations in Intrinsically Disordered Human Disease Targets
abstract: AlphaFold 3 (AF3) has transformed structural bioinformatics through generative diffusion modeling of biomolecular assemblies. However, intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs)—which comprise over 30% of the human proteome and mediate essential cell signaling, oncogenesis, and phase separation—violate the classic thermodynamic energyminimization assumptions inherent to static structure prediction.

title: An integrated strategy to obtain ready-to-use carotenoid extract from persimmon (Diospyros kaki Thunb.) using hydrophobic eutectic solvents: From virtual COSMO-SAC screening to atomistic level mechanism
abstract: Persimmon carotenoids are valuable, but the preparation suffers from the abuse of organic solvents, while the emergence of hydrophobic eutectic solvents (HESs) provides a feasible means to obtain ready-to-use extracts. This study developed an integrated strategy for the preparation and preservation of persimmon carotenoid extract using food-compatible HESs without solvent removal. Profiling identified 42 carotenoids (139.2 μg/g) in persimmon powder, with over 85% existing as esterified forms.
keywords: Artificial Neural Network And Genetic Algorithm

title: Lattice-matched SnS/SnIn4S8 heterojunction-based molecularly imprinted photoelectrochemical sensor for tetracycline detection in milk
abstract: Tetracycline residues in milk pose potential food safety risks, highlighting the need for sensitive and selective analytical methods. In this work, we developed a molecularly imprinted photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensor based on a lattice-matched SnS/SnIn4S8 heterojunction. The ultralow lattice mismatch (0.33%) promotes efficient charge separation and migration, producing a markedly enhanced photocurrent response (2.81 μA·cm-2), up to 3.6 times the responses of the individual components.

title: Alternating Copolymerization of Arynes and Aldehydes Enabled by an N -Arylamine Initiator
abstract: Here, we report the direct alternating copolymerization of arynes and aldehydes initiated by a simple N-arylamine. The N-arylamine framework is critical for suppressing competing aryne homopolymerization and promotes selective alternating polymerization through a Smiles-type rearrangement pathway. Regeneration of a neutral N-arylamine chain end during each propagation cycle enables complex polymer architectures, including block copolymers and cyclic polymers, through ring-expansion alternating copolymerization.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Direct Visualization of a Hydroperoxy Intermediate in Fluorescent Protein Chromophore Maturation in PAmCherry1
abstract: Despite the widespread use of fluorescent proteins in bioimaging, the mechanism of oxidative chromophore maturation to form the tyrosine Cα═Cβ double bond remains unclear. In the photoactivatable fluorescent protein PAmCherry1, this double bond has not yet been formed prior to photoactivation. Here, serial femtosecond crystallography (SFX) using an X-ray-free electron laser (XFEL) enabled us to capture the radiation damage-free structure of non-photoactivated PAmCherry1. This structure displayed a covalently bound hydroperoxy moiety (73% occupancy) at the sp3-hybridized Cα atom of the chromophore tyrosine residue within the imidazolinone ring. A unique hydrogen-bonding network surrounding the hydroperoxy moiety stabilizes this highly reactive chromophore species. Electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS) supported the coexistence of hydroperoxy and enolate chromophore forms. According to spectroscopic analysis, these species exist in dynamic equilibrium. MS analysis further demonstrated that photoactivation is accompanied by the formation of the mature chromophore containing a Cα═Cβ double bond together with Kolbe decarboxylation. Time-resolved SFX (TR-SFX) using a femtosecond pump laser further revealed decreasing electron density at 800 ps after photoexcitation, consistent with rapid oxidation and decarboxylation. Collectively, these results support a hydroperoxy intermediate as a key species in oxidative chromophore maturation, which is stabilized in non-photoactivated PAmCherry1.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Growth and Interface Engineering of Superconducting TiN on Sapphire by Thermal-Laser Epitaxy
abstract: Thermal-laser epitaxy (TLE) extends the accessible pressure, temperature, and growth-rate regimes of conventional molecular-beam epitaxy, enabling in situ laser annealing, high-purity buffer-layer growth, and efficient evaporation of refractory elements. These capabilities make TLE a promising platform for engineering low-loss superconducting resonators and Josephson-junction heterostructures. Here, we study the TLE growth of TiN on sapphire and observe improved transport properties with increasing growth temperature up to 1150 C. Unfortunately, we observe that the high ammonia pressure and elevated substrate temperatures required for optimal TiN properties promote reactions at the sapphire surface, resulting in voids at the TiN-substrate interface. These defects increase interfacial surface area, introduce dangling bonds, and could compromise tunnel-barrier heterostructures. We mitigate this degradation using an initial TiN seed layer grown at 850 C. With the seed layer, we achieve a superconducting transition temperature of 5.8 K, a residual resistivity ratio of 12.2, and a resistivity of 1.19 micro-ohm cm at 10 K, which, to our knowledge, is the lowest reported for TiN grown on sapphire.

title: Deep Learning-Guided Interface Engineering Stabilizes Oligomeric Enzymes
abstract: The thermostability of oligomeric enzymes is often limited by the intrinsic flexibility of subunit interfaces. Herein, we report a deep learning-driven interface engineering strategy (DeepIE) to systematically stabilize oligomeric enzymes. Applied to a dimeric formate dehydrogenase, we de novo redesigned six flexible regions at the dimer interface. The lead variant retains wild-type catalytic activity while exhibiting an ∼500-fold increase in half-life at 50 °C.

title: Searching for dark matter with the purest materials on Earth
abstract: Using bubbles, crystals, prehistoric rocks, and more, scientists look for signals from the invisible part of the universe

title: Pt Nanoparticles Supported on Ta-Doped TiO2 for Durable Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
abstract: Platinum (Pt) is more earth-abundant and corrosion-resistant than iridium (Ir), yet its deployment as an acidic oxygen anode has been abandoned due to the formation of a self-passivating, insulating PtO2 film. Here, we show that this century-old bottleneck can be alleviated by an electron-shuttling junction in which Pt nanoparticles are anchored to a tantalum (Ta)-doped titanium dioxide support, with Fermi level higher than Pt.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Magnetoelectrocatalysis at the frontier: advanced quantum materials, mechanistic insights, and application landscapes
abstract: Amid escalating environmental pollution and the urgent surge in sustainable energy demand, electrocatalysis has emerged as a key technology for sustainable energy conversion and chemical transformation. However, despite decades of progress, the rational design and development of electrocatalysts that simultaneously overcome kinetic, stability, and selectivity limitations remain central challenges.

title: Differentiating nonfluent/agrammatic and logopenic primary progressive aphasia in Catalan-Spanish bilinguals by applying multilingual multimodal machine learning (M³L) to connected speech
abstract: Background The nonfluent/agrammatic (nfv) and logopenic (lv) variants of primary progressive aphasia (PPA) disrupt fluency through distinct underlying neurocognitive mechanisms. Differential diagnosis currently requires hours of cognitive-linguistic testing, with additional barriers for bilingual patients due to a shortage of bilingual service providers and a lack of well-established assessment methods.

title: Identification of co-expressed gene sets for major molecular initiating events in rodent liver carcinogenesis using wild type and knock out rats
abstract: Liver tumors are the most common carcinogenic outcome observed in two-year bioassays used for regulatory risk assessment of chemicals and pharmaceuticals. Because these traditional long-term studies are resource-intensive and not feasible for most chemicals, there is a critical need to develop alternative approaches that can identify potential rodent liver carcinogens in short-term studies (e.g., [≤] 1 month). Biomarkers associated with molecular initiating events (MIEs) of early rodent liver tumorigenesis may enable the prediction of two-year outcomes from such studies.

title: Emergent catch bonds from slip-like contacts: cooperative force-driven proofreading at receptor--ligand interfaces
abstract: Mechanical forces modulate receptor-ligand kinetics, sometimes producing the so-called catch bond: a tensile force strengthens the bond, whereas in most cases engagement time is reduced (a slip bond). Multiple phenomenological models reproduce catch-slip behavior between receptors and ligands, primarily by positing how the reaction's free-energy landscape changes under applied forces. In this paper, we show that distinct microscopic mechanisms often collapse into mathematically equivalent multi-exponential forms.

title: Ligand-Shell-Enabled Silver Catalysis on Gold Nanoclusters for the Straightforward Synthesis of β-Naphthol Ethers from Alkynes
abstract: The use of gold chlorides alongside cationic silver is widely regarded as a standard approach for generating cationic gold in π-acid-mediated organic reactions; however, in many cases, presynthesized cationic gold alone is insufficient to catalyze such transformations. Herein, we present a rare example of employing chloride-containing gold nanoclusters to form Au–Cl–Ag reactive intermediates within protective ligand shells, enabling the isomerization/cyclization of alkynes to directly construct naphthalene rings.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Helicity Synchronization-Induced Kinetic Stabilization against Helix Inversion in Stapled Peptides: Effects of 310/α Block Sequence and Double-Stapling Topology
abstract: Communication between neighboring helical domains is central to biological function, yet dynamic interactions between distinct peptide helices remain poorly understood. Herein, we report a series of nonoverlapping doubly stapled block-type peptides composed entirely of achiral components and containing α-α, 310-310, α-310, and 310-α helical architectures. Despite their distinct geometries and hydrogen-bonding patterns, neighboring helical segments were found to communicate efficiently, resulting in exclusive formation of homochiral (P,P)- and (M,M)-helices.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Beyond Swelling: Electrochemical Doping Tunes the Balance between Ion Compensation and Exchange in a Hydrated Organic Mixed Ionic–Electronic Conductor
abstract: Organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors (OMIECs) couple electronic doping to ion compensation and water reorganization. As doping increasing, molecular reorganization within the polymer–ion–water environment is thought to underlie the often nonmonotonic response of OMIEC devices, yet this process is essential for the understanding of structure-function relationship in related OMIEC devices but remains unclear.

title: Modulation of Crystal Habit and Preferred Orientation of Aspirin: Combined Effects of Solvent and a Metallic Mesh Template during Evaporative Crystallization
abstract: Polymorphism plays a significant role in crystal engineering, as it can directly influence the physicochemical properties of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). Aspirin (ASA) is one of the extensively studied model compounds in small-molecule polymorphism due to its pharmaceutical relevance. To date, ASA has been reported to exist in four polymorphic forms, Forms I, II, III, and IV. Like polymorphism, preferred (or preferential) orientation is another important characteristic in solidform screening that increases the risk of misidentifying pharmaceutical compounds as polymorphs.

title: Ultra-thin WS2 growth by ALD from bis(tert-butylimido)bis(dimethylamido)tungsten and 1,2-ethanedithiol and detailed surface mechanism
abstract: A molecular layer deposition/atomic layer deposition (MLD/ALD) strategy using bis(tert-butylimido)bis(dimethylamido)tungsten (BTBMW) and 1,2-ethanedithiol (EDT), the latter serving as a safer organic alternative to H2S, leads to the formation of ultrathin WS2 films via a molecular/hybrid tungsten organothiolate intermediate. A multiscale approach, involving Si/SiO2 wafers, silica nanobeads, and molecular models, provides mechanistic insight into the early stages of growth.

title: Fracture mechanics favors lower-than-expected stack pressures in halide solidstate batteries
abstract: All-solid-state batteries promise safer, more energy-dense storage than cells built on liquid electrolytes. Among solid-state electrolytes, halide electrolytes offer high ionic conductivity, anodic stability, and room-temperature processability, yet stable cycling is typically achieved under stack pressures of tens to hundreds of megapascals, for reasons that remain unclear.

title: Evaluation of log D and pKa predictions for the SAMPL8 blind challenge
abstract: The goal of the Statistical Assessment of Modeling of Proteins and Ligands (SAMPL) challenge is to improve the accuracy of computational methods used in drug discovery and design by providing a platform to benchmark different methods and draw the community’s attention to specific areas of improvement. The SAMPL8 physical properties challenge focused on the prediction of pKa and log D for multi-protic compounds with two or more widely separated polar groups. Here, we present an overview of the results from the SAMPL8 challenge.

title: Not comparing like with like: a measurement-conditions audit of the solid polymer electrolyte literature
abstract: Ionic conductivities of solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) are routinely compared across publications as though they were measured the same way. We tested that assumption by building a measurement-conditions annotation layer over the largest open compilation of SPE conductivity data (16,009 measurements from 214 source papers), recording for each source study how the measurement was actually made. Fifty-eight papers spanning 1986–2020 and 20 journals were annotated across 59 fields, covering 11,394 measurements, or 71.2% of the compilation.

title: In-situ Electrochemical Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Characterization of Polymer and MXene Films
abstract: In-situ electrochemical spectroscopic ellipsometry (EC-SE) can enable real-time monitoring of optical properties and thickness changes of surfaces and thin films. This method can provide a broad range of information on the evolution of the microenvironment of an electrode during electrochemical reactions. However, to avoid modeling artifacts, accurate data analysis is critical. Here, we outline key steps in data analysis that can help prevent overfitting and misinterpretation of results.

title: Spatially resolved 3D aging model linking interdependent degradation mechanisms to knee and end-of-life prediction
abstract: Forecasting battery lifetime and degradation is valuable but difficult because lithium-ion batteries age through complex, non-linear processes. Physics-based models are often preferred for their mechanistic insight into key aging modes. This work introduces a 3D+1D electro-thermal-aging model coupling multiple degradation phenomena to capture lithium inventory loss (LLI), loss of active material (LAM), and impedance increase at the cell level.

title: Are we measuring the right thing? Evaluation practice for machine-learned transition states and reaction barriers
abstract: Machine-learned models of chemical reactivity are now reported with structural deviations below 0.1 Å, barrier errors near 1 kcal/mol and search success rates above 90 %. These figures come from different tasks, reference quantities and denominators, and this review asks what they certify. Its evidence base is five molecular datasets of small-molecule organic saddle points computed with density-functional theory, one catalysis benchmark, and the models scored on them; enzymatic, condensed-phase, photochemical and solid-state barriers are outside its scope.

title: Multimodal LLM-Assisted Diagnosis of Cryptic Failure Modes in High-Throughput Experimentation: A Case Study in Gold Nanorod Synthesis
abstract: Self-driving labs typically optimize experiments within a predefined design space. Yet high-throughput campaigns can fail for reasons outside this design space, in-cluding reagent state, stock solution quality, and handling history. Here, we present a case study of a five-plate high-throughput gold nanorod synthesis campaign in which a multimodal large language model (LLM) helped diagnose such cryptic failure modes. We used low-cost camera images for rapid assessment of seed and synthesis state, with UV–vis spectroscopy when the images were insufficient for failure diagnosis.

title: Synthesis of Dihydro-indolo-oxazines via a RedOx‑Neutral, Gold‑Catalyzed Hydride‑Transfer Process
abstract: RedOx neutral gold-mediated processes are particularly valuable for C-H bond functionalization. When these transformations proceed stepwise via intramolecular hydride transfer to an electrophilic Gold(I) center, their efficiency critically depends on the nature of the hydride donor. We report herein that, in contrast to tertiary amines, which strongly coordinate to gold and thereby tend to inhibit catalysis, benzyl ethers can serve as effective hydride donors, enabling a smooth catalytic C-H functionalization sequence.

title: QM_eMMa: An Open GPU-Accelerated Framework for Ab Initio QM/MM Molecular Dynamics and Enhanced Sampling
abstract: Ab initio QM/MM molecular dynamics can describe chemical processes accurately, but its practical use is limited by the cost of repeated electronic-structure calculations and by overhead in coupling molecular-dynamics and quantum-chemistry programs. We present QM_eMMa, an open interface that couples AMBER to PySCF/GPU4PySCF while keeping the electronic-structure engine and GPU context active throughout a simulation. The converged electronic density is reused between consecutive MD steps, with automatic recovery through a cold-start SCF calculation when needed.

title: Shaping Tumor Targeting: How Nanoparticle Morphology Influences Penetration and Accumulation in 3D Breast Cancer Models
abstract: Efficient nanomedicine delivery to solid tumors requires both tissue penetration and cellular accumulation, yet how nanocarrier architecture governs these processes remains poorly understood. Here, molecular polymer brushes spanning hydrodynamic radii (Rh) of 10–45 nm and aspect ratios of 1.2–8.1, with identical polysarcosine surface chemistry, are used to investigate transport in two extracellular matrix (ECM)-embedded breast cancer tumoroids: BT549 and MDA-MB-468 cells, separately.

title: Complementary chemical probes and substrates reveal split subsite specificity in a fungal GH12 glucanase
abstract: Xyloglucans are structurally heterogeneous polysaccharides in which xylosylation patterns vary along the β-(1,4)-glucan backbone. Because endo-glycanases engage substrates across both sides of the scissile bond, we hypothesised that GH12 substrate selectivity may vary across the catalytic cleft. We combined activity-based profiling of basidiomycete secretomes with defined fluorogenic substrates, oligosaccharide product mapping and structural analyses.

title: Unravelling concomitant pseudopolymorphs of 5,10,15,20-meso-tetrakis(4-hydroxy-3,5-dimethoxyphenyl)porphyrin: structural insight in to a guest free and two solvated forms by using MicroED
abstract: Crystal structures of three concomitant pseudopolymorphs of 5,10,15,20-meso-tetrakis(4-hydroxy-3,5-dimethoxyphenyl)porphyrin (1), comprising a solvent free form and two solvates, were elucidated by three-dimensional rotational electron diffraction (3DED/MicroED). This finding presents structural insight of 1 and highlights the potential of MicroED in resolving complex pseudopolymorphic mixtures from a single batch of sample.

title: Uncovering the Relative Importance of Chemical Emissions Arising from the Application as Polymer Additives
abstract: Polymers can act as “Trojan Horse” releasing toxic chemical additives into ecosystems and individual organisms. However, the extent to which additive use contributes to the overall emissions and environmental burdens of multifunctional chemicals remains poorly understood. Here, we use polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs), and short-, medium-, and long-chain chlorinated paraffins (SCCPs, MCCPs, and LCCPs) as case studies to quantify the contribution of polymer additive use to their global historical emissions and environmental burdens.

title: Small-supercell and Small-dataset Training Strategy of Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Point Defects
abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) can treat large-scale material systems with near first-principles accuracy and have been widely used to accelerate point-defect simulations. However, the training of MLIPs usually relies on large amounts of DFT data. This issue is particularly pronounced for charged defects, for which DFT calculations of large supercells are required to avoid long-range Coulomb interactions and finite-size effects, making the construction of datasets computationally expensive. In this work, we propose an efficient MLIP training scheme for neutral and lowly charged point defects based on small supercells (less than 100 atoms) and limited number of DFT calculations. The scheme requires only four DFT structural relaxations to construct the training dataset and the trained MLIPs dedicated for the defect can predict the defect formation energies in larger supercells (over 200 atoms) with small errors (mostly smaller than 0.3 eV). Using defects in GaN, SiO$_2$, and $\mathrm{Cu}_2\mathrm{ZnSnS}_4$ as representative examples, we evaluate the extrapolation capability of this scheme for predicting defect total energies and structural relaxations across different supercell sizes. The results show that an MLIP trained only on single small defect supercell produces severe errors when treating large supercells. Incorporating defect data from multiple supercell sizes improves the predictive performance of the MLIP, while adding pristine defect-free bulk supercells further enhances the accuracy. These results provide practical guidance for training MLIP models of defect systems with low computational costs.

title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for NV- decoherence in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters invert that attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.1-7.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies, over three decades of concentration. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts those frequencies. Were every defect on the same crystallographic site, all would shift alike and still match: worth only a factor 1.15. Real defects occupy symmetry-equivalent sites pointing in different directions, so neighbours land at different frequencies and stop exchanging: a further 2.7. What governs the coherence time is therefore the fraction of bath pairs sharing a transition frequency, not the zero-field splitting. Vacancy aggregation extends NV- spin coherence rather than shortening it.

title: Accessing Ice–Water Interfaces with Critical Curvature for Investigating Ice Nucleation at Low Supercooling
abstract: Formation of critical nuclei is the essential step of first-order phase transitions such as the crystallization of supercooled water. However, probing these nanometer-sized critical nuclei remains extremely challenging in both experiments and simulations because they form rarely and exist transiently. Here we introduce a general simulation approach, also amenable to experimental realization, that enables spatiotemporally controlled formation and long-term stabilization of critical-sized ice nuclei.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Dielectric-Screened Functionals for Cis–Trans Excitation Energies of Solvated Azobenzene Derivatives: Screening Trends in Comparison with Experiment and Published GW/BSE Calculations
abstract: Accurate modeling of electronically excited states in solution is essential for the rational design of photoactive molecular systems, but requires a reliable treatment of environmental effects. We present a mean-field approach that combines density functional theory with a polarizable continuum model (PCM) to account for environmental dielectric screening, providing an efficient mean-field alternative to higher-cost wavefunction- or many-body-based approaches. The framework employs dielectric-screened range-separated hybrid (SRSH) functionals within PCM to obtain excited states of solvated azobenzene derivatives, a prototypical molecular photoswitch. SRSH–PCM excitation energies better reproduce experiment when the larger static dielectric constant, which also accounts for nuclear polarization, is used to define long-range screening. Using the smaller optical dielectric constant, which represents purely electronic polarization, SRSH–PCM energies align better with previously reported high-quality GW–Bethe–Salpeter equation (GW/BSE) energies [Kshirsagar et al., JCTC 2020]. Our findings demonstrate that mean-field SRSH–PCM provides an effective description of excited-state properties while offering insights into the role of environmental screening and, in particular, the importance of accounting for nuclear contributions to dielectric screening in many-body calculations of solution-phase excitation energies.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Bubble detachment from circular cavities and flat surfaces
abstract: We determine the maximum stable volume of bubbles attached to flat surfaces as a function of contact radius, contact angle, and capillary length. By solving the Young-Laplace equation using a shooting method, we calculate equilibrium bubble shapes and determine when bubbles detach through three distinct modes: necking at the cavity, sideways instability, and spreading followed by necking on the surrounding surface. Our predicted detachment volumes agree well with experimental measurements of electrolytic, boiling, and carbonated bubbles, as well as pendant drops. These results bring together and extend previous analytical estimates and, by symmetry, also apply directly to pendant drops.

title: A Vanadium(II) Photosensitizer Delivered by Human Serum Albumin for Photodynamic Therapy
abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is an established clinically approved treatment; however, the development of next-generation photosensitizers remains constrained by the reliance on scarce precious-metal scaffolds and poor pharmacological properties. Earth-abundant first-row transition metals offer an attractive alternative, but their application in PDT remains underexplored.

title: Transitional Band Gaps During Polarization Switching in Wurtzite Ferroelectrics
abstract: The electronic band gap ( E g ) is commonly treated as a static materials property associated with an equilibrium crystal structure. Yet in functional materials whose operation involves field-driven structural transformations, the relevant electronic structure may evolve as the atoms traverse different configurations, with consequences for materials design and device reliability.

title: Chemical Synthesis of the endogenous metabolite Phosphocitrate and Its Structural Isomer Phosphoisocitrate
Atomic Orbital Interactions in [CeX6]2– (X = F, Cl, Br): Consequences for X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopic Analysis
abstract: Metal–ligand bonding in [CeX 6 ] 2– complexes (X = F, Cl, Br) is investigated using density functional theory (DFT) and pre-bonding analysis. The analysis quantifies atomic orbital (AO) energies and overlaps in the complexes, with a focus on the mixing between Ce 4f AOs with halide 𝑛p donor AOs. Results indicate that decreasing Ce–ligand AO overlap from X = F to Br is compensated by improved AO energy matching, leading to increased 4f-based ligand-to-metal donation across the series.

title: A bench-scale, continuous reactor for reductive polyolefin depolymerization
abstract: Catalytic deconstruction of polyolefins is central to chemical recycling, but most laboratory studies use batch reactors that obscure kinetics and limit reproducibility. Flow operation enables rigorous measurement of rates and selectivities, yet processing viscous polymer melts at small scales remains challenging. Here we present a laboratory-scale flow reactor that couples a hydraulic melt pump to a stirred-tank vessel, enabling continuous and semi-continuous operation at high pressure.

title: The first approach to highly substituted dihydroimidazotriazolones and their controlled post-transformations
abstract: A novel class of azido-modified α , β -unsaturated Ugi adducts (enamides) has been explored as a versatile platform for post -Ugi transformations. While intramolecular azide-alkyne cycloadditions of Ugi-derived peptidomimetics have been extensively studied, the corresponding azide-alkene cycloadditions on similar scaffolds have remained unexplored. In this work, we report a systematic investigation of intramolecular azide-alkene cycloaddition involving activated enamide moieties derived from Ugi adducts.

title: From Automated Beamlines to Autonomous Science
abstract: Autonomous experimentation is emerging across materials synthesis, synchrotron and neutron characterization, real-time analysis, and scientific decision-making. Yet increasingly capable artificial intelligence does not by itself create autonomous science. Scientific user facilities must also provide machine-operable experiments, machine-readable and interoperable data and interfaces, persistent provenance across the experimental lifecycle, scientific capabilities that can be discovered and orchestrated across instruments and facilities, and access models compatible with iterative experimental…

title: Direct visualization of heterogeneous molecular diffusion and interfacial barriers during condensate ripening
abstract: Ripening processes are ubiquitous in various multiphase systems, such as emulsions, crystals, alloys, and biomolecular condensates. This phenomenon significantly affects the morphology of a system and its resulting properties through the growth of dispersed domains at the expense of others without direct contact. Though ripening has been studied for centuries, a molecule-level visualization of this process has never been captured, significantly hindering our fundamental understanding.

title: Helical Polymers for Artificial Cell Engineering: Backbone-to-Droplet Reorganization in Polyacetylene-based Microdroplets
abstract: Biomolecular condensates provide a powerful framework for constructing artificial cells with crowded interiors and dynamic molecular organization. However, most synthetic condensates rely on flexible or intrinsically disordered macromolecules, leaving the role of conformationally defined synthetic polymers in liquid-liquid phase separation largely unexplored. Here, we introduce cationic helical polyacetylenes as structurally defined building blocks for coacervate-based artificial cells and investigate how their conformation governs condensate properties.

title: Collaborative Laboratory Edge Networks
abstract: Chemistry language models now predict reactions and retrosynthetic routes with useful accuracy, but they assume that proprietary reaction records can be pooled into a central cluster and that inference runs on abundant accelerators. Neither assumption holds in pharmaceutical and fine-chemical practice, where yield records cannot leave the plant network, the points of use are heterogeneous resource-limited sites, and different laboratories occupy disjoint regions of chemical space.

title: Dissecting the Roles of Optimal Tuning, Solvation, and Vibrational Corrections in Excited-State Redox Potential Prediction for Organic Photoredox Catalysts
abstract: Department of Chemistry, Emory University Abstract Reliable computational prediction of excited-state redox potentials is central to the rational design of photoredox catalysts and requires accurate treatment of both ground-state redox thermochemistry and excited-state energetics. Although time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) provides a practical computational framework, it remains unclear whether these two components should use the same range-separation treatment and how the tuning of 2 range-separated hybrid (RSH) functionals, solvent response, and vibrational corrections affect…

title: Influence of Structural Flexibility on Ion-Receptor Interactions in Octamethyl Calix[4]pyrrole Complexed with Prolinate
abstract: We present cryogenic ion vibrational spectroscopy of deprotonated L-proline ([Pro-H]-) complexed with octamethyl calix[4]pyrrole (omC4P). Density functional theory calculations reveal two low-energy binding motifs. In the lowest energy structure, the carboxylate group interacts with only three NH groups of omC4P, with the NH group of the fourth pyrrole pointing away from the binding site. In another geometry, slightly higher in energy, the ion binds to all four NH groups.

title: When the lower-barrier pathway yields the minor enantiomer: reversibility and intermediate stability in pyrroloindoline synthesis
abstract: In this work, we present a computational study that provides evidence for the origins of selectivity in the enantioselective synthesis of pyrroloindolines catalyzed by iminium ions. Through a conformational search combined with DFT calculations, we obtained the catalytic energy profile, which shows that the enantioselectivity is not determined by the barriers of the enantiodetermining C–C bond-forming step.

title: Experimental Data Analysis and Improved Cytochrome P450 Site-of-Metabolism Prediction for Drug Discovery
abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes mediate the oxidative metabolism of most marketed drugs, making early prediction of their sites of metabolism (SoMs) essential for addressing metabolic liabilities. In this work, we present a substantial update to our hybrid docking/quantum mechanics SoM prediction tool IMPACTS (J. Chem. Inf. Model., 2012, 52, 2471-2483). This update is evaluated on newly curated, fully annotated datasets containing over 2,400 datapoints and spanning nine human isoforms; these datasets are released to the community in MOL2 and JSON formats.

title: Addressing the nature and reductive stability of alkylthiol-modified Cu electrode surfaces
abstract: Cu surfaces modified with molecular adsorbates are being used in electrocatalyic processes (e.g., CO2 reduction (CO2RR)) to improve performance, but the nature and stability of molecular adsorbates (e.g. thiols) on Cu remain poorly understood owing to the sensitivity of Cu to oxidation and the complex chemical nature of the interface. To address these challenges, alkylthiol modification of 10 monolayers of electrodeposited Cu onto single-crystal Au bead electrodes has been prepared and studied using electrochemistry and in-situ fluorescence imaging.

title: Reducing Synthetic Complexity: A Fluorine-Free Benzodithiophene-Thienopyrrolodione Donor Polymer by Direct Arylation Polycondensation for Organic Photovoltaics
abstract: Synthetic complexity is a decisive aspect for absorber material availability in organic photovoltaics (OPVs). By using direct arylation polycondensation (DAP), a new route to the donor polymer PBDT-T2-TPD is presented. DAP allows to reduce the amount of toxic chemicals and simplifies the reaction scheme at the same time. Furthermore, this new route allows to vary the molar mass of PBDT-T2-TPD and thus enables the investigation of chain length-dependent OPV parameters in devices with the non-fullerene L8-BO as acceptor.

title: Why Molecular-Scale Occupancy Fluctuations Appear Gaussian without Being Bulk-Like
abstract: Molecular-scale occupancy distributions in water and hard-sphere fluids can appear remarkably Gaussian. Using classical density functional theory with an external field conjugate to the occupancy, we calculate occupancy cumulants for spherical volumes in a hard-sphere fluid and reproduce the variance and small, oscillatory third moment reported previously in Monte Carlo simulations. This agreement shows that the density functional captures the correlations responsible for the phenomenon and allows the role of excluded-volume packing to be isolated.

title: Auto-healing Co(II)-based metallosupramolecular hydrogel of 3-amino-1-propanol as Low Molecular Weight Gelator: Investigations of morphological features, rheological dynamics, and stimuli-responsiveness
abstract: In the present work, a stable, green-coloured metallohydrogel was fabricated under ambient conditions through the spontaneous self-assembly of cobalt(II) nitrate hexahydrate, Co(NO3)2·6H2O, as the metal source with 3-amino-1-propanol acting as a low-molecular-weight gelator (LMWG) in aqueous medium. The synthesized metallogel was characterized using rheological analysis i.e.; strain sweep, frequency sweep and thixotropy. Surface morphology and network texture were probed by FESEM, elemental composition was verified by EDX analysis, and the gel's stimuli-responsive were subsequently evaluated.

title: Pyrrole-Imine Dimer Stabilized Bis(germaamides) with two Ge(E)N(SiMe3)2 moieties (E = S, Se)
abstract: Bis(germaamides) and their thio- and seleno- analogs are unknown. This work reports the isolation and characterization of the first examples of thio- and seleno-analogs of bis(germaamides) 7 and 8 containing two Ge(E)NR2 moieties (E = S, Se; R = SiMe3). These compounds were obtained by oxidizing the bulky pyrrole-imine dimeric ligand-stabilized bis(aminogermylene) 5 with elemental sulfur and selenium. This study also highlights the first-ever application of the bulky pyrrole-imine dimeric ligand 3 to simultaneously stabilize two low-valent centers (germylenes or stannylenes).

title: Quantifying Validation-Induced Optimism in Machine Learning for Food Spectroscopy: An Empirical Multi-Dataset Benchmark
abstract: Background: Evaluating machine-learning regression models in food spectroscopy using random row-wise cross-validation ignores hierarchical experimental structures (replicate scans, aliquot extractions, packaging batches, instruments, and harvest campaigns). While theoretical warnings caution against sample leakage, the chemometric literature lacks a multidataset empirical quantification of validation-induced optimism, its impact on model selection, and its underlying physical mechanisms.

title: A theory of inner-sphere reorganization energy for electrocatalysis
abstract: In Marcus theory, reorganization energy links thermodynamics and kinetics for outer-sphere electron transfer, in which the redox centre exchanges an electron without changing its bonding to the electrode. Most electrocatalytic elementary steps are instead inner-sphere processes: the reacting intermediate is part of the interface, and surface bonding changes with charge transfer. A general thermodynamic definition of the full nonequilibrium preparation cost of such a bonded interface is lacking, leaving equilibrium descriptors and measured rates without a common theoretical basis.

title: Alternative synthetic pathways to selected molecular fluorophores present in citric acid-based carbon dots
abstract: Molecular fluorophores (MFs) are an integral part of many raw reaction mixtures prepared during the synthesis of carbon dots (CDs) from small organic molecules by the bottom-up methods. Despite their significant contribution to the luminescence of as-prepared CDs, the investigation of optical properties of MF is complicated by the pH dependence, possibility of formation of tautomers, low yields and complicated isolation.

title: Zeolite-Mediated Three- and Pseudo-Five-Component Reactions Involving α-Ketoglutaric Acid, Aromatic Aldehydes and 5-Aminotetrazole
abstract: We report previously undescribed multicomponent reactions of α-ketoglutaric acid, aromatic aldehydes, and 5-aminotetrazole that provides access to two distinct types of products. Notably, these transformations require the presence of 4A or 3A molecular sieves, and the formation of the target compounds is condition-controllable: the process can proceed through a pseudo-five-component pathway, yielding tetrahydropyrido[3,4-d]tetrazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidinone derivatives – the first examples of this heterocyclic framework – or can be directed toward a three-component condensation that affords…

title: DeepEnzyKat: Turnover number prediction through enzyme-substrate interaction modeling and adaptive expert ensembles
Electrochemically Hole-catalyzed Dearomative (3+2) Cycloaddition of Nitroarenes
abstract: We report the first electrochemically hole-catalyzed (3+2) dearomative cycloaddition of nitroarenes, including benzene-based derivatives. Enabled by a hole-transfer chain process, the reaction proceeds through the anodic generation of a non-stabilized azomethine ylide from a readily available precursor, providing efficient access to structurally complex pyrrolidines from a broad range of electron-deficient nitroarenes. Remarkably, full conversion is achieved using catalytic amounts of electricity (0.1 F mol-1), resulting in high TONe (222) and Faradaic efficiency (925%).

title: Multimodal Representation Learning for Exploring Natural Product Chemical Space
abstract: Natural products represent a major source of therapeutic molecules, yet their structural diversity and limited biological annotations pose substantial challenges for computational exploration and discovery. Here, we develop a multimodal molecular representation framework that integrates chemical language, molecular fingerprints, physicochemical descriptors, and molecular graphs into a unified latent space for natural product discovery.

title: Direct Alkylarene Desaturation via Base-Promoted Halogen Transfer
abstract: We report a method to prepare alkenes through the base-promoted oxidative desaturation of alkylarenes and related weakly acidic functional groups. This process operates via a tandem deprotonative-halogenation and elimination sequence using haloarene halogen-transfer reagents. The use of potassium tert-butoxide with haloarene oxidants provides a simple means to desaturate a broad range of alkylarenes, acids, esters, and amides, as well as to aromatize saturated heterocycles.

title: Redirecting Iodine Oxidation in Thyroxine by O-Phosphorylation
abstract: nachtsheim@uni-bremen.de Abstract O-Phosphorylation of a thyroxine derivative redirects mCPBA oxidation from the internal iodine to a terminal one. A two-step oxidation-hydrolysis sequence delivers the phosphate-stabilised aryl(hydroxy)iodonium salt, whose regiochemistry is established by 3 J-CP-coupling.

title: Reply to a comment ‘On the futility of the Fuoss–Kirkwood relation’ by Gradišar & Boškoski
abstract: A recent comment on our previous paper (Electrochem. Commun. 164 (2024) 107731) regarding the futility of the so-called Fuoss-Kirkwood (FK) relation presents an appreciated opportunity for clarification and further argumentation. In this reply, we provide additional arguments suggesting that the commenting authors are misguided in concluding that this relation is valid, and that, when correctly applied, the FK relation can be straightforwardly employed to derive analytical expressions of the real-valued distribution of relaxation times (DRT) for model impedances that are explicitly known in…

title: Strategic Bromine Substitution in Aryl Aminoboranes Unlocks Photochemical Route to Narrow-Band Emitting Azaborines
abstract: The development of UV/deep-blue emitters with high color purity remains a central challenge in OLED research, where conventional fluorophores suffer from broad emission and triplet-harvesting systems compromise stability. Here we show that strategic ortho-bromine substitution in bis-aryl aminoboranes unlocks an intramolecular photo-cyclization that allows direct access to azaborine frameworks under mild conditions and near quantitative yield.

title: Why Electrochemical–Thermal–Mechanical Understanding is Needed to Explain Knees in Lithium-Ion Batteries Degradation
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are essential to modern life, spanning portable electronics, electric vehicles and grid storage. Yet, their degradation mechanisms remain incompletely understood, particularly the sudden capacity drops known as knee points. In this study, commercial Samsung 50S cells are degraded under various cooling setups and charge/discharge rates, revealing consistent knees in slow-discharge cells even above 80% of initial capacity, while fast-discharge cells degraded beyond 60% without knees.

title: Interfacial Solvent Engineering of Zinc Porphyrin Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Frameworks Enables Aggregation-Enhanced Electrochemiluminescence for Synthetic Cannabinoid Sensing
abstract: Zinc porphyrin hydrogen-bonded organic frameworks (ZnTCPP HOFs) are prone to uncontrolled short-range π–π stacking at solid/liquid interfaces, which leads to aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) and consequently limits their electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency. Current strategies for suppressing ACQ primarily depend on covalent or coordination bonds and often involve laborious synthesis. Addressing this challenge from the perspective of colloid and interface science, this study introduces a chitosan (CS)–DMF counter-solvent precipitation strategy.

title: RaX-DT: An Open-Source Platform for Automated Molecular Docking Workflows and Reproducible Pipeline Validation
abstract: Automated molecular docking workflows often fail not at the scoring engine but at the interfaces between ligand preparation, protein preparation, binding-site definition, and post-processing. We present RaX-DT, an open-source, Docker Compose–deployable platform that integrates these steps in a single web application and an optional conversational assistant. RaX-DT automates 3D ligand generation, tautomer/protonation-state handling, protein cleaning, binding-site definition via P2Rank, Fpocket, or user-specified coordinates, GNINA-based docking, and interactive result visualization.

title: Designing Cure Kinetics in Polyester Networks: Tuning Initiator Content to Control Gelation and Glass-Transition Development
abstract: Unsaturated polyester networks remain widely used in composite manufacturing, construction, and infrastructure, and yet the practical relationship between initiator content and cure trajectory is not always reported consistently across industrial formulations. Using a field-representative unsaturated polyester systems, real-time gelation/exotherm were tracked with differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) to map how initiator type and content govern gel time, exotherm behavior, and the thermal state of the cured network.

title: Conformational ensembles of the TDP-43 NTD-RRM1-RRM2 domains interacting with GU-rich RNA determined by MD simulations and SAXS data
abstract: TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) is a crucial regulator of RNA metabolism whose pathological aggregation is a hallmark of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), frontotemporal dementia (FTD), and Alzheimer’s disease. Binding to GU-rich RNA sequences via its RNA recognition motifs (RRM1 and RRM2) is known to antagonize aggregation, yet the molecular mechanisms by which RNA modulates TDP-43 conformational and supramolecular organization remain poorly understood.

title: Macromolecular Size Matching in Stabilizing Corrugated Chiral Plasmonic Nanostructures
abstract: Chiral plasmonic nanoparticles derive strong chiroptical responses sensitive from their corrugated, high-curvature surfaces, but these same features are thermodynamically unstable. Surface functionalization using macromolecules could broaden their utility by enabling improved colloidal compatibility, secondary functionalization, stimuli responsiveness and and assembly into higher-order structures.

title: Investigating pH Effects on the Photoswitching of Furanyl-Indolinium Heteroarylstilbenes
abstract: Cationic heteroarylstilbenes, such as the furanyl-indolinium chromophore, represent a class of watersoluble, visible-light-responsive photoswitches. However, their photochemical behaviour under physiologically relevant pH conditions remains insufficiently understood. In this study, four derivatives were synthesized and systematically investigated, with particular emphasis on their photoswitching properties at three pH values using phosphate-buffered media.

title: Additive manufacturing of micro-architected carbide ceramics via molten salt conversion
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) enables complex micro-architected geometries in metals 1–3 , polymers 4 and oxide ceramics 4–6 , yet its extension to non-oxide ceramics remains constrained by optical opacity and high-temperature densification. Carbide ceramics are challenging for particle-based vat photopolymerization (VPP), where strong absorption limits curing, while pressure-assisted densification, often required for high density, is incompatible with delicate architectures.

title: Fiber-Scale Discrete Element Modeling Approach for Microstructural Evolution in Carbon Felt Electrode Manufacturing
abstract: Porous carbon components strongly influence transport, kinetics, and performance in electrochemical energy devices, like electrodes in redox flow batteries or gas diffusion layers in proton exchange membrane fuel cells. Yet quantitative links between industrial felt manufacturing and the resulting microstructure remain insufficiently understood. Recent studies have explored alternative bottom-up fabrication strategies to achieve greater microstructural control, while computational optimization often considers stochastic microstructures without accounting for manufacturability.

title: Performance Self-Blown Non-Isocyanate Polyurethane Foams
abstract: Rigid foams earn their place in structural applications through a specific balance of stiffness and density. Reproducing that balance without isocyanates has proven far harder than replacing the chemistry itself. Water-blown polyhydroxyurethane (PHU) foams are the most credible isocyanate-free alternatives to conventional polyurethanes, but toxic base catalysts and weak mechanical properties have stalled their adoption.

title: Quality control measurement science: Point-of-care opioid compounding and personalized pain management
abstract: Traditional "one-size-fits-all" pharmacotherapy often fails to address the complex, highly individualized needs of patients undergoing opioid tapering, pain management, and withdrawal. While distributed and point-of-care (POC) additive manufacturing—such as 3D printing, semisolid extrusion, and drop-on-demand (DoD) deposition—enable agile, patient-specific dosing and multi-drug formulations, they introduce critical quality control (QC) challenges in facilities that often lack extensive laboratory infrastructure.

title: Perovskite Photovoltaics in January-June 2026: The Certified Frontier From Cell to Module
abstract: Over an evaluation period spanning 6 months, the metal halide perovskite literature expanded by 3328 indexed publications. Of these, 884 were examined closely for physical claims, interfacial mechanisms, and stability validation across distinct device architectures. Across single junction devices, the certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) ceiling advanced to 27.6%, yet mechanistic investigations diverged over the operational function of low-dimensional capping heterostructures.

title: Enhancing Linear B-Cell Epitope Prediction via Evolutionary Scale Modeling (ESM-2) and Hybrid Feature Integration
abstract: Experimental identification of B-cell epitopes is time-consuming and resource-intensive, motivating the adoption of computational prediction approaches. This study examines the progression of sequence-based strategies by contrasting traditional machine learning methods (SVM, XGBoost, etc.) and early deep learning techniques (CNN, RNN, etc.) with sophisticated protein language models such as ESM-2.

title: Nanoscale stacking disorder and Jahn-Teller distortion in Brochantite, Cu4SO4(OH)6, revealed by 3D electron diffraction
abstract: Characterization of functional materials often neglects explicit modeling of structural disorder because of its complexity and the limitations of conventional experimental methods. Yet disorder can strongly affect material properties, and understanding its role is essential for establishing reliable structure-property relationships. Here, we address the long-standing structural complexity of brochantite, one of the most common basic copper sulfates, using 3D electron diffraction (3D ED) complemented by laboratory and synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction.

title: Black-Body-Based Scatter Removal Procedure for Quantitative Neutron Radiography at the MARS Beamline (CG-1D), HFIR
abstract: Quantitative neutron imaging is fundamentally limited by scattering artifacts, low neutron flux, and wavelength-dependent attenuation, which restrict accurate transmission measurements. This work presents the first implementation and validation of the blackbody (BB) based scatter removal procedure (Carminati et al., 2019) for quantitative neutron radiography of engineering materials at the MARS beamline (CG-1D), High Flux Isotope Reactor (HFIR), Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL).

title: Linear I···I contacts in a platinum(IV)-diiodo porphyrin: Emergent type III halogen–halogen interactions
abstract: This study presents experimental and theoretical evidence for unusual intermolecular I···I interactions between axially coordinated iodide ligands in a Pt(IV) porphyrin. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that PtI2T[3,5-diOMe]PP, where T[3,5-diOMe]PP is the 5,10,15,20-tetrakis(3,5-dimethoxyphenyl)porphyrinato dianion, crystallises in the uncommon P4/n space group, in contrast to the I4/m space group frequently observed for related metalloporphyrins, and adopts an eclipsed columnar packing arrangement, with co-crystallised dichloromethane (DCM) molecules occupying the space between…

title: LANGER: Lanthanide Affinity Network via Graph and Evolutionary Representations
abstract: The transition to sustainable energy relies heavily on rare earth elements (REEs), yet their separation remains a critical industrial bottleneck due to their nearly identical physicochemical properties. The discovery of lanmodulin (LanM), a highly selective REE-binding protein, has inspired bio-based separation strategies; however, predicting binding affinity between different LanM variants and REEs remains a significant computational challenge.

title: Synthesis and Ambiphilic Reactivity of a Monocoordinate Carbazolyl Gallylene
abstract: Monocoordinate Lewis base-free gallium(I) complexes are rare due to their high propensity for disproportionation and oligomerization. Herein, we report the synthesis and structural characterization of a monomeric, monocoordinate gallylene stabilized by a bulky 1,8-bis(3,5-ditert-butylphenyl)-3,6-di-tert-butylcarbazole ligand. Taking advantage of the substantial kinetic shielding provided by the flanking aryl substituents, the compound can be isolated as a solvent free, one-coordinate main-group carbenoid.

title: Study of neutron-induced effects on cultural heritage linen fabrics using fluorescence spectroscopy
abstract: This study investigates how the fluorescence of linen changes when it is irradiated with a focus for the first time on the distinction between neutron from pure gamma ray irradiation. Earlier studies showed that when linen was subjected to both neutron and gamma irradiation, its visible and ultraviolet (UV) fluorescence increased as the radiation dose increased. However, the spectroscopic reason was not explained, and the specific contributions of neutrons versus gamma rays were not addressed.

title: Crowding-induced interfacial aggregation underlies enzyme concentration-dependent inhibition during poly(ethylene terephthalate) depolymerization
abstract: Enzymatic depolymerization of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) using PET hydrolases (PETases) offers a sustainable route for plastic recycling, yet high enzyme loadings paradoxically reduce degradation efficiency. The molecular basis of this enzyme concentration-dependent inhibition (ECDI) has remained unresolved. Here, by exploiting host-dependent differences in folding quality of a sequence-identical PETase, we show that ECDI is driven by crowding-induced interfacial aggregation, which progressively destabilizes PET-bound enzymes.

title: Cuban Bentonite/Polymer Nanocomposites: A Sustainable Alternative for Food Packaging
abstract: The environmental impact of conventional polymers has driven the search for sustainable food packaging alternatives. Clay incorporation into polymers matrices has shown to enhance optical, mechanical, and barrier properties. This study evaluates Cuban natural bentonite as a reinforcing phase in hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC), carboxymethylcellulose (CMC), polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), plus their mixtures (PVA/PVP and PVA/CMC).

title: Towards Universal Calibration for Infrared Spectroscopy with Probabilistic Interference Removal
abstract: Structured interferences from substrates, matrices, and instrumental artifacts in mid-infrared (IR) spectra often overlap with analyte features and introduce errors in quantitative analysis. Existing correction methods rely on heuristic parameter selection and frequently perform suboptimally when applied across a diverse set of samples. We present a probabilistic framework, Variational-Inference-based Background Elimination in Spectroscopy (VIBES), for automated estimation of regularization hyperparameters from the data that enables removal of such interferences.

title: Report – 4th Ontologies4Chem Workshop
abstract: The Ontologies4Chem workshop series brings together developers and users of chemical ontologies to align ontology initiatives with shared standards and approaches to semantic interoperability. The 4th Ontologies4Chem Workshop, organized by TIB in collaboration with the Beilstein-Institute, the NFDI4Chem Consortium, the NFDI4Cat Consortium, and the Physical Sciences Data Infrastructure (PSDI) took place from November 11 to 13, 2025 in Limburg an der Lahn (Hessen, Germany).

title: Carbonylative Cross Couplings Promoted by a Metal Carbonyl Complex in Catalytic Amounts
abstract: Carbon monoxide is a highly valuable building block that enables the rapid construction of complex molecules like pharmaceuticals from simple and commercial precursors. However, the handling of CO requires special and elaborate precautions, since it is a highly toxic and odourless gas supplied in pressurized gas cylinders. To improve operations with carbon monoxide several CO surrogates including Mo(CO) 6 have been introduced, which form CO in enclosed gas reactors on demand.

title: Large Language Models in Chemistry and Materials Science: A Comprehensive Survey
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are expanding the scope of artificial intelligence in chemistry and materials science by connecting scientific knowledge, heterogeneous data, computational tools, and experimental workflows. This article presents a comprehensive survey of the foundations, representations, methods, applications, and evaluation of LLM-centered scientific systems.

title: Certified Zero-Frequency Response and a Fourth-Order Mechanism Test for Nonlinear Soft-Constrained Langevin Dynamics
abstract: Eliminating stiff internal coordinates can preserve equilibrium while changing kinetics, and a finite-time coarse-graining error does not by itself control a zero-frequency transport observable. We study a reversible overdamped Langevin model with constant microscopic mobility and nonlinear soft constraints, Uϵ(x, y; γ) = V (x− Fγ) + |y − g(x)|2 2ϵ , where V may be nonquadratic and nonconvex. An exact coordinate transformation factorizes the equilibrium measure but produces a nontrivial kinetic metric.

title: Neutron Crystallography Maps the Interaction Landscape of Pseudomonas aeruginosa LecA with Deuterated Aromatic β-Galactoside
abstract: Aromatic derivatives of β-galactosides are potent inhibitors of the LecA lectin, a key virulence factor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, involved in host recognition, tissue adhesion and biofilm formation. This opportunistic bacterial pathogen is considered a serious global health threat, particularly due to the emergence of multidrug-resistant strains. Anti-adhesive and anti-biofilm compounds represent promising alternatives or complements to conventional antibiotic therapies. The design of such pathoblockers requires detailed structural insights into their interactions with the target protein.

title: Antimicrobial Resistance Breakers That Specifically Restore Efficacy of Polymyxins
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global threat to human health and prosperity. Antimicrobial resistance breakers (ARBs), molecules that reverse AMR e.g., by blocking enzymes involved in bacterial membrane remodelling, are an attractive solution to restore the efficacy of existing antibiotics. We have identified several hits from in silico screening that restore polymyxin B (PmB) efficacy at concentrations of 250-500 µM in the clinically relevant ESKAPE pathogen Enterobacter bugandensis. The compounds act in tandem with PmB, but not with other antibiotics.

title: A conformational filter protocol for structures with topological symmetry
abstract: This paper presents an efficient conformational filter protocol for handling structures with topological symmetry implemented in the open-source molecular modelling program curcuma. This approach addresses the challenge of comparing molecular conformations in which symmetrically equivalent atoms may have different indices in the structure files. Descriptors that are independent of the storing order of the atoms (energy differences, rotational constants, and Vietoris-Rips (VR) persistence barcodes) are used to efficiently predict potential structural similarities before performing…

title: Exploration of Low-Crystalline NiPd(CN)4 by Ab Initio Global Structure Search
abstract: For poorly crystalline inorganic materials, it is often difficult to uniquely determine the crystal structure from diffraction measurements alone. In this study, we identified the crystal structure of a newly synthesized metal cyanide NiPd(CN) 4 by combining experiments with ab initio calculations. The observed powder X-ray diffraction pattern could not be explained by any previously reported analogous structures, while magnetization measurements indicated the presence of a finite local magnetic moment in the ground state.

title: Aged Hops Increase 3-Methyl-2-butene-1-thiol (MBT), β-Ionone, and Branched-Chain Esters in Beer
Group-Invariant Certificates and Solvers for Diversity Selection in Combinatorial Libraries
abstract: Selection of massive, mutually non-redundant subset of highly scoring compounds from a combinatorial library is a standardized design in early stage drug discovery. It is usually solved by heuristics that return a ranking of capable candidates, however there is no quality guarantee. We formulate and introduce a method as maximum weighted independent set with a parameter soft redundancy penalty on a Cayley graph over the abelian group ℤ𝑛, 𝑞—where 𝑛 is the number of substitution positions and 𝑞 the number of substituents per position.

title: Computational Fluid Dynamics-Informed Machine Learning-Enabled Digital Twin for Vapor Maldistribution Prediction in Structured Packed Distillation Columns
abstract: Vapor maldistribution in structured-packed distillation columns reduces separation performance. While experimental measurements are essential for characterizing column hydrodynamics, they often lack the resolution to capture velocity distributions or to systematically quantify how column geometry and operating conditions affect vapor maldistribution throughout the packed bed.

title: Cooperative Electronic Programming by Phenanthroline Pockets, Ethynyl Bridges, and Pyrene Cores in a One-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework for Chemoselective Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer molecular precision, yet their catalytic function is often treated as though the metal center operates independently of the scaffold that surrounds it. Here, we introduce TU-24, a one-dimensional COF in which phenanthroline pockets, ethynyl bridges, and pyrene cores are deliberately integrated to co-program coordination geometry, frontier electronic structure, and reaction progression for nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis.

title: Revealing tilt-driven structural heterogeneity in hybrid improper ferroelectrics by spatially-resolved crystallography
abstract: Domain walls in ferroic oxides can host emergent functionalities that differ fundamentally from those of the surrounding bulk, making their microscopic structure central to understanding and controlling macroscopic behaviour. We use scanning three-dimensional X-ray diffraction to map the spatial evolution of coupled octahedral distortion modes across ferroelastic domain walls in the hybrid improper ferroelectric Ca$_{2.15}$Sr$_{0.85}$Ti$_{2}$O$_{7}$. By combining tomographic reconstruction with symmetry-adapted analysis of the octahedral rotation and tilt and associated strain modes, we map their spatial evolution across individual walls in the bulk crystal. We find that the walls are intrinsically extended, with widths far exceeding those expected for conventional Ising-like ferroic interfaces. The wall structure is characterised by a continuous rotation of the tilt order parameter through a tetragonal intermediate. These results provide new microscopic insight into the structural mechanisms governing ferroelastic wall formation, ferroelectric switching, and emergent functionality at domain walls.

title: Axial thermal expansion from free-energy minimization with temperature-dependent force constants in phonopy: a technical report, with $α$- and $ω$-Ti as the worked example
abstract: In a hexagonal crystal the $a$ and $c$ axes change their lengths at different rates with increasing temperature, and the thermal expansion is described by two coefficients, one for each axis. The equilibrium lattice parameters at each temperature are found by minimizing the Helmholtz free energy over the lattice parameters, and the coefficients are their logarithmic derivatives with respect to temperature. This report describes a procedure for this minimization as implemented in phonopy. The free energy is computed with harmonic force constants at a finite set of values of $a$ and $c$, and a free-energy surface over $a$ and $c$ is fitted to these values. In a variant, the harmonic force constants are replaced by temperature-dependent force constants from a self-consistent harmonic approximation, with the forces computed by a machine-learning potential fitted at each of these values. The $α$ and $ω$ phases of titanium are the worked example. Both calculations give negative thermal expansion of the $c$ axis of $α$-Ti at low temperature and none in $ω$-Ti, and they differ most for the $c$ axis of $α$-Ti. The axial coefficients are harder to compute than the volumetric one, because the two axes are coupled in the free energy. In both phases of titanium the thermal effect that lengthens $a$ also shortens $c$. The coefficient of the $c$ axis is then the sum of two terms of opposite sign that partly cancel, and a small error in either term gives a large relative error in the coefficient. The report measures how much each setting of the procedure changes the thermal expansion coefficients, with the $c$ axis of $α$-Ti as the most sensitive case.

title: Amorphous insulating MoS$_x$ films deposited by magnetron sputtering as a low-index optical coating
abstract: While much effort are now concentrated on exploration of crystalline form of MoS$_2$ as a two-dimensional material, we show that room-temperature DC magnetron sputtering from pressurized MoS$_2$ powder target produces amorphous MoS$_x$ films with optical properties fundamentally different from those of crystalline MoS$_2$. The films were found to have a sulfur content of approximately $x=1.8$, indicating sulfur deficiency. They are optically isotropic and exhibit rather low optical losses, with a refractive index of about 2 over the visible and near-infrared spectral range. Their compatibility with lift-off lithography and dry etching makes amorphous MoS$_x$ a promising material for integrated photonic applications.

title: Adapting Boltz-2 with limited experimental activity data improves early enrichment in virtual screening
abstract: Virtual screening aims to prioritize active compounds from large chemical libraries within a limited experimental budget. When applying Boltz-2 to virtual screening, a key challenge is how to use limited experimental data from the target assay to improve the prioritization of active compounds. We investigated whether fine-tuning the Boltz-2 affinity heads with a small number of binary activity labels could improve early enrichment of active compounds in hit discovery. We compared fine-tuning with 40-300 labels in a retrospective evaluation on eight MF-PCBA targets. With 300 activity measurements, fine-tuning increased the number of actives in the top 1% by a geometric mean of 1.77-fold across the eight targets and improved average precision (AP) by 2.14-fold relative to the control without fine-tuning. We also investigated whether rescoring a subset of candidates could retain the improvement in hit recovery by reranking only the top-ranked Boltz-2 candidates with the fine-tuned head. Restricting rescoring to approximately 10% of the evaluation set retained hit recovery comparable to full rescoring. These findings show that affinity-head fine-tuning with limited activity labels improves early enrichment with Boltz-2 and that this benefit can be retained when rescoring a restricted set of candidates.

title: Plasma ATR-FTIR spectroscopy combined with machine learning for nasopharyngeal carcinoma classification
abstract: BackgroundNasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is often diagnosed at advanced stages, creating a need for minimally invasive approaches to support detection. This study evaluated plasma attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy, combined with machine learning, to distinguish NPC from clinically healthy individuals.MethodsPlasma samples from 51 histologically confirmed NPC cases and 51 age- and sex-matched clinically healthy controls were analyzed across 4000-600 cm-1. Differences at 21 spectral peaks were assessed using the Mann-Whitney U test.
venue: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy

title: Enhanced thermal conductivity of (010) (AlxGa1-x)2O3 epitaxial films utilizing indium-catalyzed molecular beam epitaxy
abstract: (AlxGa1-x)2O3/beta-Ga2O3 transistors are an emerging candidate for high-power and high-frequency electronic devices. beta-Ga2O3 in particular is notably limited for anisotropic low thermal conductivity, which is further reduced in (AlxGa1-x)2O3 due to alloy and other defect-driven phonon scattering mechanisms. In this work we show that the thermal conductivity of (010) oriented (AlxGa1-x)2O3 thin films for 0.01 < x < 0.20, measured using time-domain thermoreflectance (TDTR), is limited by alloy scattering without observable adverse scattering by additional defects. This is enabled through the synthesis of the (AlxGa1-x)2O3 films using molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) on \b{eta}-Ga2O3 substrates, leveraging indium-catalyzed growth to suppress dislocation formation and phase separation to achieve single-phase pseudomorphic films up to x = 0.2. This growth process improved the thermal conductivity of (AlxGa1-x)2O3 by 2X as compared to previously reported values. For increasing Al composition (x), we observe a steady decline in (AlxGa1-x)2O3 thermal conductivity due to alloy scattering which is validated using virtual crystal approximation (VCA) model. We also show that the thermal boundary conductance across the Al/(AlxGa1-x)2O3 interface is reduced with increasing x, which we posit is due to the stiffening of the (AlxGa1-x)2O3 acoustic modes with increasing x by comparing experimental results with a diffuse mismatch model (DMM). Overall, these thermal characteristics provide valuable insights for designing heterostructures with optimized interfaces and composition.

title: FlashBoB: I/O-Efficient Exact Backward-over-Backward for Softmax Attention
abstract: Transformer models built on the attention mechanism have become a central building block in modern deep learning, yet softmax attention remains a major bottleneck for long-context workloads. While FlashAttention makes the forward and first backward passes I/O-efficient, it does not support backward-over-backward (BoB), which enables exact differentiation through the backward pass for applications such as second-order optimization, test-time training, gradient-based memory, and meta-learning. Existing BoB implementations either materialize large intermediate tensors or exhaust GPU memory at long sequence lengths. We present FlashBoB, an exact, I/O-efficient algorithm for BoB in softmax attention that keeps computation within on-chip tiles and avoids all $N \times N$ intermediate tensors, where $N$ is the sequence length. The key insight is a hierarchical affine structure in the softmax double backward: two row-wise scalars determine all outputs through affine transformations. This yields a two-pass schedule with bounded on-chip static random-access memory (SRAM) usage and minimal off-chip high-bandwidth memory (HBM) traffic. FlashBoB achieves $Θ(N^2 d^2/M)$ HBM traffic ($d$ is the head dimension and $M$ is the memory size) and, within the standard FlashAttention-style score-recomputation model, matches the inherited large-cache lower bound for exact forward attention. Empirically, it scales exact attention BoB to $N=262\text{K}$ on a single A100 80GB GPU, where prior PyTorch exact baselines fail by $N=16\text{K}$, and is up to $6.3\times$ faster than FlashBack. These results make exact second-order attention practical at long-context sequence lengths where prior implementations cannot run efficiently.

title: From Heuristics to Machine Learning: The Performance Ceiling for Single-Ion Magnets and Its Electronic Origin
abstract: Machine learning (ML) is expected to speed up the discovery of single-ion magnets (SIMs), but does the structural information available before synthesis allow such predictions? For 1215 lanthanide complexes from the SIMDAVIS 1.2.1 database we compared three increasing levels of structural description: tabular features of the coordination site, continuous symmetry measures of the coordination polyhedron, and the complete 3D arrangement of atoms. All three converge to an accuracy near 76%, only slightly above the 71% of the single rule "predict SIM for Dy3+". To explain the failures, we combined multireference ab initio calculations with an inspection of the structures behind the high-confidence errors. The SIMs missed by the geometric models are field-induced relaxers whose ground Kramers doublets are prone to tunnelling, a property invisible to geometric descriptors. Many false positives contain several lanthanide centers or radicals, so their relaxation is collective and outside the single-ion picture. The electronic-structure and connectivity information needed to identify SIMs is therefore not accessible to geometric methods alone. Geometric models remain useful: restricting the screening to compounds with high prediction confidence raises the accuracy to 88% while retaining 48% of the dataset. Building on the analysis of the failures, we propose a strategy that combines simple filters for nuclearity and for radicals with ligand-field descriptors from ab initio calculations.

title: RamanOmics decodes the spatial vibrational-molecular architecture of senescence in aging and repair
abstract: Aging and tissue repair involve heterogeneous remodeling across transcriptional, biochemical and cellular dimensions, yet prevailing definitions rely on isolated molecular markers that obscure how these states co-evolve. Here we present RamanOmics, a multimodal framework integrating label-free hyperspectral Raman imaging with single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to link biochemical states with transcriptional programs at single-cell spatial resolution. Applied to young and old mouse lung and skin, RamanOmics reveals tissue-specific programs: lung senescent cells are enriched for extracellular matrix remodeling and transforming growth factor-β signaling, whereas skin senescence is dominated by epidermal differentiation genes (Krt10, Lor and Sbsn). Across tissues, we identified a conserved lipid-linked Raman signature (1,131-1,135 cm-1) marking p21+ senescent cells and developed a machine learning-derived, multimodal barcode enabling nondestructive senescence identification in situ. In a mouse wound-healing model, RamanOmics reveals reactivation of epidermal differentiation genes (Krt10, Lor and Sbsn) in senescent cells, alongside increased lipid-associated Raman signatures. Together, RamanOmics provides a tissue-agnostic framework for scalable, multimodal profiling of cellular states.

title: The Loading-Dependent Evolution of Ru Cocatalysts on CdS Nanorods for Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution: Unveiling the Critical Role of Neighboring Single-Atom Site Engineering
